# Module `network`

network - TCP/IP socket basics over BSD sockets.

Everything crosses the runtime's `__vyb_net_*` functions in
`runtime/vyb_runtime.c`; the Vyb surface stays allocation/pointer-free. IP
addresses are plain strings: a dotted-quad ("127.0.0.1") or a colon-hex IPv6
literal ("::1"). Pass "0.0.0.0" (or ""), or "::" for IPv6, to bind any
interface. A port of `0` asks the kernel for an ephemeral port, which you can
read back with `socket_local_port()`. `socket_set_timeout(fd, ms)` keeps a
non-responsive peer from hanging a caller forever.

Usage (loopback echo):
  import network::{socket_open, socket_bind, socket_listen, socket_accept,
                   socket_connect, socket_send, socket_recv, socket_local_port,
                   socket_close, Socket}
  srv = socket_open(Socket::AF_INET, Socket::SOCK_STREAM, 0)
  socket_bind(srv, "127.0.0.1", 0)
  socket_listen(srv, 1)
  port = socket_local_port(srv)
  cli = socket_open(Socket::AF_INET, Socket::SOCK_STREAM, 0)
  socket_connect(cli, "127.0.0.1", port)
  conn = socket_accept(srv)
  socket_send(cli, "hello")
  socket_recv(conn, 5)   // "hello"

Diagnostics: `socket_error_code()` (0 = no error) and `socket_error_message()`
report the result of the last network operation.

<a id="sym-socket_set_timeout"></a>
### `socket_set_timeout` · fn

```
socket_set_timeout(fd<Int>, ms<Int>)<Int> ->
```

Put a read + write timeout on a socket so a hung peer can't block the process
forever; `ms` of 0 (or negative) disables the timeout. Returns 0 on success.

<a id="sym-tcp_accept"></a>
### `tcp_accept` · fn

```
tcp_accept(listener<TcpListener>)<TcpStream> ->
```

Accept the next pending connection on `listener`. Returns the new TcpStream,
or one with fd == -1 on failure (blocking accept; see async_tcp_accept for the
event-loop variant).

<a id="sym-tcp_listen"></a>
### `tcp_listen` · fn

```
tcp_listen(ip<String>, port<Int>, backlog<Int>)<TcpListener> ->
```

Listen on `ip:port` ("" or "0.0.0.0" = all interfaces; port 0 = ephemeral,
read back with local_port(listener)). Returns a TcpListener, or one with
fd == -1 on failure.
